c4ff7780a4.q: What was Tommy Baru's car accident in 2013 and how did it lead him to personal injury law?
c4ff7780a4.a: In 2013, while leaving work from bartending at Essence Fest in New Orleans, Tommy Baru was rear-ended on the interstate by a car traveling at 100 miles per hour, which caused the vehicle to flip multiple times. He was ejected from the car, broke his neck, and split his head open. This traumatic experience, combined with his mother-in-law's guidance as an experienced paralegal in personal injury, led him to shift his career focus from his original goal of criminal law to personal injury law.
c4ff7780a4.e: From Car Accident Survivor to Personal Injury Attorney
c4ff7780a4.rq: I'm trying to put personal back into personal injury because those guys you see on TV, those guys in the suits, those guys who post all over the billboards—99% of those guys have not even gotten in a car wreck, much less been catastrophically injured like I have.

35eef37baa.q: What is Tommy Baru's approach to hiring and scaling his law firm?
35eef37baa.a: Baru prefers to keep his team small, currently employing a paralegal and office manager (a former adjuster with paralegal experience) plus an assistant. He deliberately avoids scaling to multiple attorneys because he wants to maintain quality customer service and avoid becoming the "machine" that large firms represent. He is hesitant to hire associates unless they demonstrate unique thought processes, bring their own cases and client load, and share his entrepreneurial ambition rather than simply seeking salary and benefits.
